To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the electrocatalytic activity for water reduction is lower for SDLC than for Pt, and the exchange current density increases with the H2/H2O ratio.
the reduction of water on SDLC is slower than on Pt.

1) SDLC is not a suitable electrode for water reduction at high temperature; 2) SDLC is a better electrode than platinum for water oxidation; 3) SDLC has a higher charge transfer activation energy than platinum; 4) The overvoltage for water reduction is higher over SDLC electrodes than platinum.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the electrochemical reduction of oxygen at the cathode of the Solid Oxide Fuel Cell (SOFC) and with the electrochemical kinetics of such process.
the electrochemical behaviour of the SDLC/YSZ interface, which is one of the most promising materials in the field of intermediate temperature fuel cells.

the development of a new type of electrocatalytic electrode based on the use of a mixed ionic and electronic conducting (MIEC) material as a cathode in high temperature electrolysis cells for hydrogen production from water.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
SDLC is less active and less selective than platinum in the water splitting at temperatures ranging from about 700°C to about 1000°C.

the water reduction at SDLC/YSZ interfaces is a process which, at low current densities, is controlled by a charge transfer process with an activation energy higher than that of the platinum/YSZ interfaces.
the SDLC cathode is less efficient than Pt, although the former is a promising candidate for the cathodic side of a solid oxide fuel cell.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the electrochemical behaviour of SDLC/YSZ interfaces is similar to that of platinum/YSZ interfaces.
the SDLC/YSZ cathode appears to be a promising alternative for the use in SOFC applications, but further improvements are required to reach the performances of the platinum based electrodes.

the SDLC/YSZ interface is not suitable for the water reduction at temperatures lower than 800°C, while at higher temperatures it may be considered a viable alternative to platinum, although it is still less efficient.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the water reduction at SDLC/YSZ interfaces is a charge transfer rate-determining process, which is more difficult than that of platinum, but the exchange current densities are still high, of the order of 10 -3 A/cm 2, and therefore the SDLC/YS Z interface could represent a promising cathode material for high temperature SOFCs.
SDLC seems to be less active than platinum for the water reduction at high temperature.

, although the SDLC/YSZ cathode has a lower performance than the Pt/YS Z interface, the SDLC is a promising cathode for the SOFC, since it can be prepared at lower temperatures than Pt/YSZ and is more resistant to carbon deposition.
